learningObjective: Understand triton.autotune: key-based caching, Config parameters, and the limits of the search.

canonicalClaims.claim: `triton.autotune` measures each user-listed Config once per distinct `key` tuple, caches the winner, and reuses it for future launches with the same key. Configs bundle tile-size constants plus `num_warps` and `num_stages`.
nonImplications: Does not imply the search is exhaustive over all possible configs.
Does not imply the cache is persistent across processes by default.

misconceptions.claim: Autotune exhaustively searches all possible (BM, BN, BK, num_warps, num_stages).
misconceptions.whyWrong: It only tests the user-provided list.

misconceptions.claim: Autotune runs only at compile time.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is invoked on first launch of each new key tuple, at runtime.

misconceptions.claim: `num_warps` is a free-form runtime argument the caller passes at each launch.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is fixed per Config in the autotune list.

misconceptions.claim: Autotune guarantees optimal selection under noise.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Measurement variance can pick a suboptimal config.

implementationFacts: `key=['M','N','K']` re-tunes when any of these change value.
In-memory cache; TRITON_CACHE_DIR can persist compiled kernels but not autotune choices by default.
